figures: Bamakhepa (Bamacharan Chattopadhyay, 1837–1911), the 'mad saint' of Tarapith, Birbhum
Kailaspati (Kailashpati) Baba — tantric guru who initiated Bamakhepa
Mokshananda — tantric preceptor who, with Kailaspati, installed Bamakhepa as Tarapith's spiritual head
Maharani of Natore — temple patron whose dream legitimized feeding Bamakhepa before the deity
Nanda Handi — untouchable-caste leper devotee healed by Bamakhepa
Vashistha — legendary sage of the Panchamundi asana at Tarapith
Krishnananda Agamavagisha — 16th-c. author of the Brihat Tantrasara (Dashamahavidya digest incl. Tara)
John Woodroffe (Arthur Avalon) — translator/editor of Tantratattva, Hymns to the Goddess, Mahanirvana Tantra
Jogindranath Chattopadhyay — author of the 1926 Bengali hagiography Bamakshepa
Tarakhepa — disciple through whom Bamakhepa supported the freedom movement

texts.title: Bamakshepa (বামাক্ষ্যাপা), 4th ed.
texts.notes: Hagiography by Jogindranath Chattopadhyay; Digital Library of India scan explicitly tagged 'In Public Domain'. Primary printed record of the oral Bamakhepa lore.

texts.title: Tarapither Sadhak (তারাপীঠের সাধক), 2nd ed.
texts.notes: Bhabesh Dutta's hagiography of the Tarapith sadhak; free scan on archive.org but copyright status unverified (author death date unknown) — treat as in-copyright.

texts.title: Tarapith Bhairav
texts.notes: Sushil Kumar Bandyopadhyay's hagiography of Bamakhepa as the Bhairav of Tarapith; 1969 publication — in copyright, not public domain.

texts.title: Mahapith Tarapith
texts.notes: On the great pitha and its Tara tradition; DLI scan, copyright status unverified — not confirmed public domain.

texts.title: Tantrikaguru Bamakhepa
texts.notes: Odia hagiography by Jayaguru Das; rights unverified — not public domain.

texts.title: Bamakhyapa (2026 upload)
texts.notes: Recent user upload (creator 'Pankaj') on archive.org; rights unverified — not public domain.

texts.title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story
texts.notes: Kali Mandir article excerpted from Kali: The Black Goddess of Dakshineswar (E. U. Harding, Nicolas-Hays, 1993, pp. 274–281). Copyrighted — events paraphrased; quotes kept to one short sentence each (fair use).

texts.title: Mad Saint Bama Khyapa — Son of Maa Tara
texts.notes: Pradyot Roy's blog, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 — free to read but not public domain; paraphrased, single-sentence quotes only.

texts.title: Tantrasara (Brihat Tantrasara) of Krishnananda Agamavagisha
texts.notes: Bengal's great Dashamahavidya digest (synthesis of 170+ tantras) that informs Tarapith's Tara worship; scan of an old print (partly missing pages). Author d. 16th c. — the text is public domain.

texts.title: Tararahasya
texts.notes: Jivananda Vidyasagara's Calcutta edition of the Tararahasya, a classic Shakta Tara text; 1896 print — public domain.

texts.title: Brihat Nila Tantra
texts.era: c. 1923 edition (Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies)
texts.notes: Madhusudan Kaul's edition of the Nila Tantra — the primary tantra of Ugra-Tara/Neela Saraswati worship behind Tarapith's fierce Tara form; early-20th-c. print of a classical text — public domain.

texts.title: Mahanirvana Tantra (1884 Vidyasagara ed.)
texts.notes: Jibananda Vidyasagara's Sanskrit edition; frames Shakta doctrine for the Bengal tradition; 1884 — public domain.

texts.title: The Great Liberation (Mahanirvana Tantra), trans. Arthur Avalon
texts.notes: Avalon's classic translation; Woodroffe d. 1936 — public domain.

texts.title: Principles of Tantra (Tantratattva), ed. Arthur Avalon
texts.notes: Tantratattva of Siva Chandra Vidyarnava; contains the Tara and Ugra-Tara mantra/dhyana sections used in Tarapith-style sadhana; authors d. 1914/1936 — public domain.

texts.title: Hymns to the Goddess and Hymn to Kali, trans. Arthur Avalon
texts.notes: Includes the Tarastakam and other Tara hymns from the tantras; 1913 — public domain.

texts.title: Shakti and Shakta, Sir John Woodroffe
texts.notes: Essays on Shakta doctrine and ritual incl. the Tara worship context of Tarapith; Woodroffe d. 1936 — public domain.

texts.title: Todala Tantra
texts.notes: The dashamahavidya source text listing Tara (already used in the project's remedial mapping). The text is classical/public-domain, but NO standalone verified scan was located during this research — stated explicitly, not guessed.

teachings.topic: Compassion before ritual (feeding the hungry first)
teachings.paraphrase: The hungry are the Mother's own children: feeding them comes before any ritual offering. A heart that puts another's hunger before its own rite pleases the Goddess most.
teachings.quote: If my son does not eat first, how can I, his mother?
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: Single-pointed absorption in the Divine, indifferent to worldly competence and reputation, is not madness but the sign of a great soul.
teachings.quote: One who is called khepa is generally considered a great soul.
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: Healing requires no fee, ritual or worthiness test; Bamakhepa cured a leper with mud and a dying man by feeding him with his own hand.
teachings.quote: Bamakhepa took pity on him and fed him with his own hand.
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: No one is untouchable to the Mother; the Brahmin-born saint accepted food from a leper of the untouchable caste, beyond all thought of purity and impurity.
teachings.quote: the thought of purity or impurity did not enter his mind
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: Dwelling amid corpses and burning pyres dissolves the fear of death, which underlies every other fear; the shmashan is the Mother's own home.
teachings.quote: I live in the cremation ground with my Mother.
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: He owned almost nothing and walked naked like Shiva and Tara, his parents; freedom and fearlessness grew from total non-attachment.
teachings.quote: My Father (Shiva) is naked; my Mother (Tara) is also naked.
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: Elaborate ritual and scriptural learning are unnecessary; consistent devotion and faith of mind and soul are sufficient for true worship of the Mother.
teachings.quote: only consistent devotion, faith of mind and soul is enough for worshiping
teachings.source_title: Mad Saint Bama Khyapa — Son of Maa Tara (tarapithtemple.blogspot.com)

teachings.topic: Celibate tantra — every woman is the Mother
teachings.paraphrase: Tantric power needs no licence; Bamakhepa completed all major tantric rites in strict celibacy, seeing every woman as the Mother, like Sri Ramakrishna.
teachings.quote: Bamakhepa, like Sri Ramakrishna, practiced Tantra while remaining absolutely celibate.
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: Whatever power works through a devotee belongs to the Mother alone; the true sadhaka claims neither credit for healing nor blame for outcomes.
teachings.quote: I am not responsible, for it was the Mother who spoke through me.
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: Mocking the saint for sharing food with stray dogs, the proud saw the dogs become gods in a vision — divinity dwells equally in every creature.
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.paraphrase: Spiritual standing was spent on others: he fought for temple servitors' wages, cleared villagers' taxes with disciples' gifts, and funded the freedom struggle through Tarakhepa.
teachings.quote: He also contributed a significant portion of people's donation to the freedom struggle through his disciple named Tarakhepa.
teachings.source_title: Mad Saint Bama Khyapa — Son of Maa Tara (tarapithtemple.blogspot.com)

teachings.paraphrase: Even the 'mad' saint surrendered to his gurus, completing all major tantric rites under Kailaspati Baba and Mokshananda before receiving authority.
teachings.source_title: Sri Bamakhepa of Tarapith — A Brief Life Story (kalimandir.org)

teachings.topic: The fierce Mother is the loving Mother
teachings.paraphrase: Tara's terrifying form hides a mother's heart: the Goddess appeared to Bamakhepa in her ferocious aspect and drew him to her breast.
teachings.quote: Maa Tara gave a vision to Bama khepa in the cremation grounds in her ferocious form and then pulled him close to her chest.
teachings.source_title: Mad Saint Bama Khyapa — Son of Maa Tara (tarapithtemple.blogspot.com)

teachings.topic: The Divine as family (Bado Maa / Choto Maa)
teachings.paraphrase: Devotion matures when the Goddess is loved as family; Bamakhepa called Tara his elder mother and longed to feed her with his own hand.
teachings.quote: He addressed Maa Tara as 'Bado Maa' (the elder mother) and his own mother as 'Choto Maa' (the younger mother).
teachings.source_title: Mad Saint Bama Khyapa — Son of Maa Tara (tarapithtemple.blogspot.com)

suggested_skills: compassion-first-routing: open every consult with immediate practical relief (the hungry are fed first) before any esoteric content
non-discrimination-policy: treat every seeker equally regardless of caste, class or gender signals; no purity-based filtering of requests
fearless-safety-gate: refuse harmful magic (marana/vashikarana) without exception and offer Shanti/Paushtika/Raksha instead — extend the existing C++ SafetyValidator
healing-support-referral: health or distress queries get supportive words plus referral to professional care; never diagnose
simple-living-reply-style: plain-language, jargon-free, concise answers; strip ritual pedantry
bhakti-core-persona: devotion over procedure — offer minimal-effort practice alternatives (name, flower, water) to complex ritual requests
lineage-citation-store: embed this source-cited teaching pack in the C++ knowledge module so every persona claim carries title + URL
shmashan-fear-meditation: mortality-contemplation module (Bamakhepa's cremation-ground sadhana) for fear-of-death counseling
community-service-prompts: periodically route users toward concrete acts of service and charity, mirroring his tax-relief and freedom-struggle giving
